references.text: The same chapter describes how touching dead animals makes a person unclean until evening, and that the clothes must be washed.
Parallel text about uncleanness from touching carcasses and the requirement to wash clothes and remain unclean until evening.
Similar regulations about washing clothes and being unclean until evening upon contact with unclean things.
Concerns those who eat animals that died naturally or were torn apart, requiring them to wash their clothes and bathe.
Prohibition against eating animals that died naturally, emphasizing that such animals make a person unclean.
Prohibition against eating meat torn apart by wild animals.
Ezekiel refers to never having eaten carrion or torn flesh, pointing to purity laws.
Similar cleansing ritual involving washing clothes and remaining unclean until evening after contact with the dead.
